newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resid prices jump with crude, weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resid prices jump with crude, weather.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices moved higher again Wednesday in moderate activity, boosted by a sharp NYMEX crude rally and cold East Coast weather that has left resid somewhat cheaper than gas, industry sources said.
"With crude up and gas firm, resid prices are moving up," said one cash trader, noting cold weather has stirred better rack and utility demand.

In New York Harbor, physical one percent firmed 50 cents to $20.00-25 a barrel, with December paper quoted slightly higher early at $21.00-25, then sold later at $21.50 with bidders left over at that number, traders said.
NYH 0.3 percent low pour jumped 75 cents to about $23.50 on reports 50,000 barrels of Nov 20-30 LP sold late Tuesday at $23.50 but was now offered at $24, traders said.
High sulphurs in NYH gained about 50 cents with crude and firm bunkers, with 2.2 percent now quoted at $19.25-50.
At the U.S. Gulf, activity was quiet, but one percent sellers raised their sights by a quarter to $18.25, while three percent was up 25-50 cents to about $17, traders said.
USG December three percent paper also firmed slightly, with bidders now at $17.50 or better.

New York City gate swing gas gained another dime or so to about the $3.55/mmBtu mark versus one percent resid at a $3.20/mmBtu equivalent. December gas in New York was still talked in the $3.90s/mmBtu compared to NYH December one percent resid paper at a $3.41/mmBtu equivalent.
